summary: Control exact ordinary Aico widgets and retained owner roots, create roots, and observe or administer pinned roots.

help:
Usage: st aico create REQUEST_ID [PROMPT] --tool claude-code|codex|pi|agent-hub --work-role ID [--blank-slate | --project PROJECT --project-root PATH] [--instructions PROMPT[@REVISION]] [--resume-session SESSION_ID]
       st aico create REQUEST_ID PROMPT --tool agent-hub --agent SLUG --work-role ID --project PROJECT --project-root PATH [--model MODEL]
       st aico widget status|title|coordinator [OPTIONS]
       st aico root status|title|end|send REQUEST_ID [OPTIONS]
       st aico sessions [--owner-socket PATH]
       st aico roots [REQUEST_ID] [--watch SECONDS]
       st aico admin REQUEST_ID [clear|submit] [OPTIONS]
       st aico placement --needs mem=6G,cpu=2[,cap=live-ready] [--pool NAME]
       st aico wake TIME "NOTE" | list | cancel WAKE_ID
       st aico wait session|job|reply|run|ask|host|tap REF [--until ...] [--timeout 2h] [--block]
       st aico nudge KIND REF
       st aico waits [--recent]
       st aico watch LANE_ID | list
       st aico unwatch LANE_ID

create: one exact owner root with transient sanitized prompt; --blank-slate starts a fresh empty workspace without first-party context for Claude Code, Codex or Pi; optional native Claude Code, Codex or Pi resume in a newly allocated root. roots: compact verified identity and advisory TUI status; bounded watch. admin: pinned request; currently fails closed because native atomic idle/draft/thread control is unavailable. widget/root: exact owner view controls, root end, and root send (one generation-pinned follow-up into a running coordinator-created root). Output contains metadata only. Receipts: applied:false means nothing was applied; applied:null means unknown, so reconcile with status before any retry.

Window verbs are retired (`layout`, `widget position`, `root position`, `root show`): Aico has no desktop windows any more; each prints that and exits 2.

Follow-ups to coordinator-created roots (Blank Slate and Pi included): st aico root send. Other native message delivery remains sessions send/verify: exact UUID + stable source revision; queued/durable does not prove consumption or slash execution.

sessions lists all current Tether catalog sessions, including ordinary/unlinked Aico widgets and coordinator-created roots, with exact widget IDs and ownership/state metadata. roots covers retained coordinator-created roots only.
help.create:
Usage: st aico create REQUEST_ID [PROMPT] --tool claude-code|codex|pi|agent-hub --work-role ID [--blank-slate | --project PROJECT --project-root PATH] [--instructions PROMPT[@REVISION]] [OPTIONS]

--tool TOOL is required: claude-code, codex, pi or agent-hub. Tether refuses any other tool with unsupported_tool and names the ones it accepts. Each tool runs the model in its own config. --resume-session SESSION_ID resumes an exact saved Claude Code, Codex or Pi session (lowercase UUID) in a new owner root; no picker, latest-thread inference or terminal input. Default --role portfolio-root. New roots require --work-role ID: coordinator, implementation, research, review, recon, hunting, operations or other. The fixed work role is separate from opaque --role metadata; no parent inheritance. --work-role-name is an optional display name. Resume keeps the native session's original work role; legacy retries may omit the field and remain Unknown. --lead-root and --facet are optional opaque metadata. PROMPT or --stdin supplies <=2000 sanitized UTF-8 bytes; no secrets or framing controls. For a longer brief, write it to a file and pass a short prompt naming its path (not "$(cat FILE)", which hits the same cap); the error names which check failed. Resume without either uses a fixed post-crash reconciliation prompt. Fresh create requires a prompt. --blank-slate needs no --project or --project-root and keeps only native harness instructions plus silent command guards. It also turns off Codex plugins, apps and MCP servers, so a Blank Slate Codex root cannot see the owner's Chrome through the ChatGPT Chrome extension. For an owner-selected Chrome tab, launch without --blank-slate, or have the agent use st browser selected-tabs list and --selected-tab HANDLE (any tool, Blank Slate included; the owner grants the tab with the SummitFlow Selected Tab extension). --instructions PROMPT[@REVISION] adds an Agent Hub prompt revision to the agent's instructions (REVISION: an id or unique prefix from st prompt revisions PROMPT; default: the revision holding the current content). Tether keeps the snapshot for the session's restarts, resume and reboot restore; a Blank Slate session gets only these. It shows as '· prompt@revision' in the session title.

Reuse the same REQUEST_ID and complete body after an uncertain response. A pending root that host admission deferred shows launch (reason, nextRetryAt, attempts); Aico tries it again itself every 30 s. Matching retries reconcile the same root; changed body conflicts; ended requests remain tombstones. Output is bounded content-free metadata. No catalog prompt retention or fleet ledger; sessions emit/wait apply only to fleet-started roots. Creation requires an already running owner; Aico shows its new root. --host HOST starts the root on a remote agent host from ~/.config/tether/hosts.json (agent-work), powering it on first if it is off; --project-root is the host's path, which mirrors this computer's (/srv/workspaces/projects/<project>). It shows in Aico like a local session, with the host's name. --host auto --needs mem=6G,cpu=2[,cap=live-ready] lets Tether pick the first host whose live room fits (free memory minus the host's reserve and other sessions' holds) and holds the needs there until the session ends; no host fits = at_capacity with one reason per host, nothing started. cap=live-ready needs a host whose proxy selftest marker still matches its fingerprint. --pool NAME (with --host auto) picks only from that pool in ~/.config/tether/placement.json pools; without it the default pool, which never includes a pooled host. st aico placement --needs ... [--pool NAME] shows where auto would start it, with each host's room or reason, and starts nothing. --root-socket PATH selects an exact Tether socket. No deployment or owner startup. Run from an Aico session (AICO_WIDGET_ID, read from the nearest ancestor process when a harness filters shell env), create sends it as launchedBy and Tether records lineage: the new root joins the launcher's coordinator, or the launcher becomes a coordinator. Output includes launchedBy.

Codex launches accept --model MODEL and --reasoning-effort EFFORT. --daybreak on|off overrides Daybreak for this launch; omit it to inherit the user setting. These are per-launch overrides, including exact resume; they do not change shared defaults. The selected Codex CLI validates model availability and effort support. Reuse the complete selection with the same request ID on retry. For fresh context, end the old coordinator-created root and create a new request with its followup brief and explicit model/effort.

Pi launches require --model PROVIDER/MODEL and accept --reasoning-effort off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max. The owner passes separate native --provider/--model flags and --thinking. Pi supports exact UUID resume with --session in the original working directory. Use that original --project-root; a UUID from another directory enters native fork confirmation and creates a new UUID if confirmed. --daybreak on|off also supports Pi with --model openai/gpt-6-sol. Aico passes Pi --approve internally on fresh launch to trust the selected project; do not pass --approve to st aico create. A fresh Pi root starts under a session ID Tether picks, so crash recovery and reboot restore can resume it. --agent-hub-context on|off controls optional Pi context; required policy and ingestion remain active. Follow up a running Pi root with st aico root send REQUEST_ID TEXT --generation SHA256 (same model and context); end the exact root and create another request when the instruction needs fresh context.

--tool agent-hub starts a chat session on an Agent Hub agent, not a terminal: --agent SLUG is required (and refused for other tools), --model MODEL optionally overrides the agent's model (Tether refuses an unknown agent or model with unknown_agent or unknown_model, and an unreachable Agent Hub with agent_hub_unavailable). The prompt is posted as the first turn, and create exits nonzero (reason turn_not_started, detail with Agent Hub's words) when Agent Hub stores the prompt but cannot run it, such as a working directory it refuses; repeat the same REQUEST_ID to post it again. --blank-slate gives the chat an empty workspace under /tmp/aico-blank-slate, the scratch Agent Hub accepts, instead of a project (--project-root is then not needed; --project defaults to agent-hub, since Agent Hub only knows registered projects). Resume, --reasoning-effort, --daybreak and --agent-hub-context do not apply. Run from an Aico session, the chat shows as that coordinator's child like any other root. Follow up with st aico root send (a new turn, or queued until the running turn ends with queued:true; nonzero with reason and detail when Agent Hub cannot run it), read st aico root status REQUEST_ID (turnState running, idle or unknown, queued count and the last turn error) or watch st aico roots REQUEST_ID (terminal busy while a turn runs, turn_finished when idle), end with st aico root end (cancels the turn and closes the Agent Hub session). It has no terminal, so show, position and window controls do not apply yet.
help.sessions:
Usage: st aico sessions [--owner-socket PATH]

List all current Tether catalog sessions, including ordinary/unlinked Pi and Codex widgets and coordinator-created roots. Output includes exact widget ID, ownership/coordinator, tool, project/title, workload status and agent state. Includes retained sessions with no visible window; ended sessions are omitted by Tether. Read-only; no terminal content, input, focus changes or owner startup. Uses the current Tether instance; --owner-socket selects an exact control socket.
help.roots:
Usage: st aico roots [REQUEST_ID] [--watch SECONDS] [--interval SECONDS]

Omit REQUEST_ID to discover running coordinator-created roots only. Ordinary widgets are omitted; use st aico sessions for the full session inventory. An exact ID can also report a retained unavailable root. Snapshot JSON contains identity/status only; --watch (>0, <=3600 seconds) emits baselines and changed states only. Poll interval defaults to 2 seconds (minimum 0.1). Discovery is bounded to 128 catalog entries and 256 KiB; snapshots have a 10-second bound. Identity races fail closed and watches never re-pin. Unknown/unsupported TUI profiles are ambiguous/unavailable. An agent-hub root reports its Agent Hub turn state (busy, turn_finished, or ambiguous when Agent Hub cannot be reached) with backend:agent-hub. GUI/owner absence is unavailable; this command never starts Aico.

Native-thread delivery is separate: exact bound UUID + stable --source-key revision, <=2000 sanitized UTF-8 bytes. Passive default. A queued/durable receipt does not prove working/consumption and has no process-generation fence. Terminal admin capability is exposed separately by admin; execution currently fails closed.
help.admin:
Usage: st aico admin REQUEST_ID [clear|submit] [OPTIONS]

Omit the operation to inspect the owner capability. clear/submit require --generation SHA256 --thread UUID --request-key KEY. submit also requires --stdin (<=2000 UTF-8 bytes; no framing controls). Reuse the same request key after an uncertain response.

Currently fails closed: native atomic current-thread + idle/empty-draft/input fence and idempotent receipt are unavailable. Returns concise content-free metadata; never sends tmux input, captures text, retries Enter, or changes permissions. An uncertain transport reports applied:null. --root-socket PATH selects an exact private owner socket.

Quick path: followups to coordinator-created roots use st aico root send (generation-pinned paste + Enter, not this atomic admin operation); other agents use sessions send/verify. Recycle a coordinator-created root with root end, verify ended, then create a new request with the brief and explicit model/effort. No operator tmux input or desktop focus is needed.
help.widget:
Usage: st aico widget status [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]
       st aico widget title "Name" [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]
       st aico widget coordinator on|off [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Control one exact ordinary Aico widget in the Aico session list. Omit --widget-id to use the exact AICO_WIDGET_ID from this managed pane; missing or invalid identity fails closed. IDs require 8 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Each mutation reads the exact widget immediately first, sends its current generation, and verifies the returned identity and generation. No fleet/root discovery or native-thread inference. GUI absence is unavailable; this command never starts Aico. Output contains identity/status metadata only, never label content. applied:false means a qualified refusal or no request; applied:null means the outcome is unknown; reconcile with status and never blindly retry.
help.widget status:
Usage: st aico widget status [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Read one exact ordinary widget descriptor through Tether's private socket. Defaults to this managed pane's AICO_WIDGET_ID; an explicit --widget-id selects only that exact 8-character lowercase hexadecimal ID. Missing/invalid identity fails closed. Output contains owner/widget/session/generation/status/availability metadata only.
help.widget title:
Usage: st aico widget title "Name" [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Rename the exact ordinary widget using its immediately read current generation. Defaults to AICO_WIDGET_ID; no selection or thread inference. Supply a non-secret control-free single-line label of 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes. Content goes only to the owner's existing session metadata; receipts and errors contain no label. Missing, unavailable or stale generations fail closed.
help.widget position:
Usage: st aico widget position X Y WIDTH HEIGHT [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Retired: Aico has no desktop windows any more; sessions show in Aico web. Nothing to arrange or show.
help.widget coordinator:
Usage: st aico widget coordinator on|off [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Mark (on) or unmark (off) the exact ordinary widget as a coordinator using its immediately read current generation. Defaults to AICO_WIDGET_ID. A coordinator shows a Coordinator label in Aico web. The mark persists across Aico restarts. Missing, unavailable or stale generations fail closed.
help.root:
Usage: st aico root status REQUEST_ID
       st aico root title REQUEST_ID "Name" [OPTIONS]
       st aico root end REQUEST_ID [OPTIONS]
       st aico root send REQUEST_ID TEXT|--stdin --generation SHA256 [OPTIONS]

Control one exact retained owner root (direct st aico create or fleet-started) by request ID. Mutations read the exact descriptor first, require running status, pin its generation, send one request and verify identity and generation in the receipt. Non-running roots fail closed. Uses Tether's private socket (--root-socket pins an exact one). Stored roots with owner a-term are still read. No fleet event, prompt or label retention; never starts an owner. For fleet roots prefer sessions close so the fleet ledger records End.
help.root status:
Usage: st aico root status REQUEST_ID [--root-socket PATH]

Read one exact retained root descriptor: owner, request, host and logical identity, surface locator, generation and status (running, pending, uncertain or ended). No terminal or label content.
help.root show:
Usage: st aico root show REQUEST_ID [--root-socket PATH]

Retired: Aico has no desktop windows any more; sessions show in Aico web. Nothing to arrange or show.
help.root title:
Usage: st aico root title REQUEST_ID "Name" [--root-socket PATH]

Rename the exact running root using its immediately read generation. Supply a non-secret control-free single-line label of 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes. Content goes only to the owner's existing session metadata; receipts and errors contain no label. st sessions title is a compatibility alias.
help.root position:
Usage: st aico root position REQUEST_ID X Y WIDTH HEIGHT [--root-socket PATH]

Retired: Aico has no desktop windows any more; sessions show in Aico web. Nothing to arrange or show.
help.wake:
Usage: st aico wake TIME "NOTE"
       st aico wake list
       st aico wake cancel WAKE_ID

Schedule a check-in on this Aico session (AICO_WIDGET_ID; --widget-id ID for another). At TIME, Tether pastes "[Scheduled check-in for 5:30 PM] NOTE" into the agent once it is idle and nobody is typing. TIME is HH:MM (next occurrence, local time), +30m / +2h / +1h30m, or ISO 8601. Closing the session tab keeps it; ending the session cancels it unless the owner keeps it. Claude Code, Codex and Pi sessions whose state Tether knows, and Agent Hub sessions. Lanes you launch report finished, blocked and ended on their own; don't schedule check-ins for them. Waiting on something else? st aico wait (st aico wait time is this command); use a check-in only for follow-ups that really are about time.

Example: st aico wake +1h "check the release"
help.wait:
Usage: st aico wait session ID|REQ [--until finished|idle|blocked|ended] [--timeout 2h] [--note T] [--key K] [--block]
       st aico wait job|reply|run|ask|host|tap REF [--until STATE] [--timeout 2h] [--note T] [--block]
       st aico wait time WHEN NOTE
       st aico wait get WAIT_ID [--block]
       st aico wait cancel WAIT_ID
       st aico waits [--recent]
       st aico nudge KIND REF

Know when something you wait on is ready instead of checking at a guessed time. Arm the wait and end your turn: you get one line when it is ready, e.g. [Ready] session "Store lane" (req neri-r1) finished · st aico root status neri-r1, or [Wait timed out] ... after the timeout (default 24h, at most 7d), never silence. Something already ready fires at once.

Kinds and --until (first is the default):
  session ID|REQ   finished (a turn ended after your last root send to it), idle, blocked (permission prompt or input needed), ended. An already-ended session fires at once.
  job ID           done: a SummitFlow service job (st service rebuild ... --detach prints it; full id or unique prefix) succeeded, failed or was interrupted, with its exit code.
  reply REQ        acked or closed: a coordination request you sent (st sessions send; the 6-hex request id) was answered, or closed or withdrawn.
  run ID           finished or needs-you: an Agent Hub run Tether follows.
  ask ID           answered: an owner ask (tether ask create).
  host NAME        connected: a hub host is back.
  tap ID           decided: a Nightshift tap (the 32-hex notice id) was approved or denied.
Tether reads each from its owner when it changes, every 60 s and at start. nudge KIND REF asks it to re-read at once (a hint; it changes nothing); use it right after you change the thing yourself.

--note adds your words to the line; --key returns the armed wait this session set with that key (session waits only). Lanes you launch report on their own; don't wait on them. Subagents, Workflow agents and agents outside Aico: --block in a background shell holds the command and prints the line (exit 0 ready, 4 the session ended first, 3 timed out, 2 Tether unreachable; st aico wait get WAIT_ID --block picks it up again); a session wait from a Codex subagent is refused not_main_agent. A Tether older than these kinds refuses them with wait_kind_unsupported. cancel is quiet and confirms. wait time = st aico wake (only for follow-ups really about time). JSON output; applied:false is a refusal with reason and detail.

Example: st aico wait session neri-r1 --timeout 2h --note "merge its branch"
Example: st aico wait job 66d97c21 --note "check the deploy"
help.nudge:
Usage: st aico nudge KIND REF

Ask Tether to re-read one thing waits watch (KIND: session, job, reply, run, ask, host, tap) at once instead of at its next look. A hint only: it changes nothing and arms nothing; armed waits on it fire if it is now ready. Output: {kind, ref, armed} (armed = how many waits watch it). See st aico wait --help.
help.waits:
Usage: st aico waits [--recent] [--widget-id ID]

List this session's armed waits (AICO_WIDGET_ID), oldest first; --recent adds the ones over in the last day with their line. See st aico wait --help.
help.watch:
Usage: st aico watch LANE_ID [--widget-id ID]
       st aico watch list

Lane reports: a lane started with st aico create tells whoever launched it, as one pasted line, when it finishes a turn (to its launcher), is blocked on a prompt or ends (to the root coordinator and the launcher), e.g. [Ready] lane "Store lane" finished after 6m · st aico root status REQ. Nothing to subscribe. watch adds this session (AICO_WIDGET_ID) as a receiver of another lane's reports, also one nobody launched; list shows your watches and unwatches. Output is JSON with hears: lineage (you hear it already), watch or none. Refused: self_watch, watch_cycle (you already report to that lane, e.g. it is your coordinator).
help.unwatch:
Usage: st aico unwatch LANE_ID [--widget-id ID]

Stop hearing a lane's reports in this session (AICO_WIDGET_ID), also ones lineage would send you. st aico watch LANE_ID undoes it. Output is JSON with hears: none.
help.root end:
Usage: st aico root end REQUEST_ID [--root-socket PATH] [--owner-socket PATH]

End the exact root's workload with its immediately read generation. It uses Tether's session End containment contract (--owner-socket pins an exact socket) and accepts only an ended receipt. An ended tombstone reports applied:false and sends nothing. Blocked cleanup or lost transport reports applied:null: reconcile with root status, never relaunch. Fleet roots: prefer st sessions close.
help.placement:
Usage: st aico placement --needs mem=6G,cpu=2[,cap=live-ready] [--pool NAME] [--root-socket PATH]

Shows where st aico create --host auto would start a session with these needs now, with each host's room or reason. Starts and reserves nothing. --pool NAME picks from that pool in ~/.config/tether/placement.json pools; default: the default pool. An unknown pool is refused with unknown_pool and the pool names.
help.root send:
Usage: st aico root send REQUEST_ID TEXT --generation SHA256 [--root-socket PATH] [--owner-socket PATH]
       st aico root send REQUEST_ID --stdin --generation SHA256 [OPTIONS]

Queue one follow-up into the exact running root a coordinator created (Claude Code, Codex, Pi or Agent Hub chat, Blank Slate included; an Agent Hub chat takes it as a new turn, or queues it until the running turn ends and adds queued:true). --generation is required: the generation last read from st aico root status. A restarted, replaced, ended or unknown root, or a host session that is not that workload, refuses with applied:false (stale_generation, workload_unavailable, not_found) and sends nothing. Then Tether's generation-fenced inject sends one bracketed paste and one Enter under the session lock; a busy TUI queues it as steering, an idle one starts a turn. Model, effort and context are unchanged. TEXT or --stdin: <=2000 UTF-8 bytes, tab and newline only, no credentials. Success is applied:true delivered:true with a byte count, never the text. Delivered means the pane received it, not that the agent consumed it; watch st aico roots REQUEST_ID. applied:null (lost transport after sending) may have delivered: check the root's screen or transcript before resending, since a paste has no idempotency key. Does not exclude a human typing in the same pane.

usage.when: list Aico/Tether sessions, including ordinary widgets omitted by roots
precautions: Read-only catalog metadata; includes widget IDs, ownership/coordinator, tool, project/title, workload and agent state. No terminal text, input or focus changes.
Current Tether instance only; includes retained sessions with no visible window and omits ended sessions. Failure or an oversized response is reported, never a partial inventory.

usage.cmd: st aico create REQUEST_ID [PROMPT] --tool claude-code|codex|pi|agent-hub --work-role ID [--blank-slate | --project PROJECT --project-root PATH] [--instructions PROMPT[@REVISION]] [--resume-session SESSION_ID] [--model MODEL] [--reasoning-effort EFFORT] [--daybreak on|off] [--agent SLUG]
usage.when: create a new owner root (a terminal agent, or --tool agent-hub --agent SLUG for an Agent Hub chat) or explicitly recover one exact saved Claude Code, Codex or Pi session after a crash
precautions: Owner resume adapters validate exact lowercase native UUIDs for Claude Code, Codex and Pi. Pi requires an explicit provider/model per launch. New root launch; never paste into an existing pane or choose latest/picker entries.

Prompt is sanitized and bounded to 2000 UTF-8 bytes; put a longer brief in a file and name its path in the prompt. No secrets, transcript or fleet ledger. sessions emit/wait apply only to fleet-started roots. Default recovery prompt reconciles state before continuation.

Declare one fixed --work-role at launch; a different role requires a new native session or a fitting existing one. Reuse request ID and full body on retry; conflicts fail closed, ended roots remain tombstones. Running proves workload presence, not authenticated model readiness or prompt completion.

usage.when: read compact identity/status for existing Aico catalog roots or watch bounded status changes
precautions: Read-only; no terminal/draft text. One-time verified owner/server/pane discovery; identity races fail closed and watches never re-pin.
Visible TUI status is advisory, not objective completion. Unknown profiles are ambiguous/unavailable; GUI/owner absence is unavailable.

Instruction delivery uses sessions send separately: passive default; native-thread requires exact UUID + stable revision and <=2000 sanitized UTF-8 bytes. Queued/durable does not mean working/consumed and is not generation-fenced.

usage.cmd: st aico admin REQUEST_ID [clear|submit] --generation SHA256 --thread UUID --request-key KEY [--stdin]
usage.when: inspect or request Aico-owned native terminal administration at an idle scope seam
precautions: Currently fail-closed; the native atomic thread/idle/draft/input operation and idempotent receipt are unavailable.
No terminal input/capture or retry. Text enters only bounded stdin; output is content-free. Reuse the same request key after an uncertain transport.

usage.when: read the current ordinary Aico widget identity and availability before widget controls
precautions: Defaults to exact AICO_WIDGET_ID from the current managed pane; explicit --widget-id requires 8 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Missing or invalid identity fails closed; no fleet/root or native-thread inference.
Tether's private socket only; no desktop capture/input or owner startup. Mutations read the exact descriptor immediately first and verify identity and generation in the receipt.
Labels require 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes of non-secret control-free single-line Unicode. Output contains no label.

usage.when: rename the current ordinary Aico widget through its owner
precautions: Defaults to exact AICO_WIDGET_ID from the current managed pane; explicit --widget-id requires 8 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Missing or invalid identity fails closed; no fleet/root or native-thread inference.
Tether's private socket only; no desktop capture/input or owner startup. Mutations read the exact descriptor immediately first and verify identity and generation in the receipt.
Labels require 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes of non-secret control-free single-line Unicode. Output contains no label.

usage.when: read one exact retained root's identity, generation and status
precautions: Exact retained request ID only; no focused/recent selection, fleet discovery or native-thread inference. Mutations read the descriptor immediately first, require running status and verify identity and generation in the receipt.

Owner sockets/routes only; no desktop capture/input or owner startup. applied:false is a qualified refusal or no request; applied:null is unknown, so reconcile with root status and never blindly retry.
Labels require 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes of non-secret control-free single-line Unicode. Output contains no label.

usage.when: rename one exact running retained root through its generation-fenced owner route
precautions: Exact retained request ID only; no focused/recent selection, fleet discovery or native-thread inference. Mutations read the descriptor immediately first, require running status and verify identity and generation in the receipt.

Owner sockets/routes only; no desktop capture/input or owner startup. applied:false is a qualified refusal or no request; applied:null is unknown, so reconcile with root status and never blindly retry.
Labels require 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes of non-secret control-free single-line Unicode. Output contains no label.

usage.when: end one exact retained root's workload through the owner's generation-fenced End contract
precautions: Exact retained request ID only; no focused/recent selection, fleet discovery or native-thread inference. Mutations read the descriptor immediately first, require running status and verify identity and generation in the receipt.

Owner sockets/routes only; no desktop capture/input or owner startup. applied:false is a qualified refusal or no request; applied:null is unknown, so reconcile with root status and never blindly retry.
Labels require 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes of non-secret control-free single-line Unicode. Output contains no label.

usage.cmd: st aico root send REQUEST_ID TEXT --generation SHA256
usage.when: follow up one exact running coordinator-created root (Blank Slate, Pi) without changing model or context
precautions: Stale or ended generation: applied:false, nothing sent. Delivered is a queued paste + Enter, not consumption; after applied:null check the screen before resending. <=2000 bytes, no secrets.

usage.cmd: st aico wake TIME "NOTE" | list | cancel WAKE_ID
usage.when: schedule a check-in on your own Aico session for a follow-up that is really about time (lanes you launch report on their own)
precautions: Own session by default (AICO_WIDGET_ID). TIME: HH:MM, +30m/+2h or ISO 8601. Pasted once the agent is idle with an empty input line.
End cancels it unless the owner keeps it. JSON output; applied:false is a refusal with reason and detail.

usage.cmd: st aico wait KIND REF [--until S] [--timeout 2h] [--block] | waits | wait cancel ID | nudge KIND REF
usage.when: know when a session, job, reply, run, ask, host or tap is ready instead of a timed check-in; lanes you launch report on their own
precautions: Arm it and end your turn: one line when ready or timed out, never silent.
Subagents: --block in a background shell.
nudge re-reads at once (hint only).

usage.cmd: st aico watch LANE_ID | list; st aico unwatch LANE_ID
usage.when: hear (or stop hearing) another lane's finished, blocked and ended reports in your own session; lanes you launched report to you already
precautions: Own session by default (AICO_WIDGET_ID); LANE_ID is the lane's eight-hex session id. Reports arrive as one pasted line once you are idle, never the lane's reply text.
self_watch and watch_cycle are refused. Output is JSON; applied:false is a refusal with reason and detail.
